extracted.intended_audience: prospective Documenters; community journalists; organizers; educators; curious citizens interested in attending and reporting public meetings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for people who attend, document, and publish coverage of local public meetings (notetaking, live reporting, audio, and multimedia) to build a public record and support local accountability. Emphasizes training, payment, community practice, and making meeting coverage useful to journalists, organizers, educators, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: We’re putting every public meeting on the record
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re putting every public meeting on the record in Documenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's core aim: ensure meetings are documented and publicly accessible. This frames the expectation that coverage should create an accessible, persistent record of what occurred at public meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: train and pay hundreds of people to attend under-reported public meetings and publish the results
rubrics_metrics.description: We train and pay hundreds of people to attend under-reported public meetings and publish the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard: Documenters should be trained and compensated; reporters are expected to attend meetings (especially those that lack media attention) and produce publishable outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep tabs with regular notes, real-time social media updates, and multimedia reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep tabs with regular notes, real-time social media updates, and multimedia reports from Documenters in your area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formats and cadence expectation: coverage should include regular meeting notes, live or real-time social media updates for immediacy, and multimedia (audio, photos, video) for richer documentation and wider access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include meeting metadata, role, and reporter attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Meeting listings show city, topical category, date, meeting title/body, role (Notetaking / Live reporting / Audio), and the reporter's name (e.g., 'Notetaking by Jinlu Yuan').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting outputs should include clear metadata (location, date, committee/meeting name, topical tag), the type of coverage produced (notetaking, live reporting, audio), and bylines/attribution so readers can identify who reported and what format is available (linking to 'See the report').

rubrics_metrics.name: Show how tax dollars are spent; show what elected officials are doing; show whether they are listening; show the process
rubrics_metrics.description: "How are your tax dollars spent? What are your elected officials doing? Are they listening to you? What is the process? That, as a Documenter, is what you have to show people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive accountability criteria: reporting should answer concrete civic questions about budgets/spending, elected officials' actions, public responsiveness, and procedural mechanics—providing evidence and explanation that helps the public understand government decisions and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover meetings with little or no other media presence
rubrics_metrics.description: "In almost every case for a meeting that I’ve covered, I’ve been the only person connected to the media that has been in the room."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority: seek out and cover under-reported meetings where other media are absent or scarce, filling gaps in local reporting and ensuring those meetings enter the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a new public record
rubrics_metrics.description: Together, we’re building a new public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective-impact standard: individual reports should cumulatively contribute to a comprehensive and searchable public record of civic meetings and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make coverage useful to journalists, organizers, educators, and curious citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: About City Bureau’s Documenters Network — Journalists: How our public meeting coverage supports local reporting. Organizers: How our public meeting coverage tracks policy trends and public input. Educators: How our training modules build civic knowledge and action. Curious Citizens: How anyone can become a Documenter in one of our local programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience-purpose alignment: produce coverage that serves different stakeholder needs — source material and leads for journalists, trend- and input-tracking for organizers, curricular/training resources for educators, and accessible entry points for everyday citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in community of practice; attend workshops; develop skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Get involved in our community of practice. Find upcoming workshops. Become a Documenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process and quality-improvement expectation: contributors are encouraged to join trainings and the community practice to develop notetaking and reporting skills, share standards, and improve the consistency and usefulness of meeting coverage.
